item.title: Tottenham outcast Richarlison convicted of running red light in £60k sportscar
item.description: Tottenham Hotspur forward Richarlison has received a court fine after being caught driving through a red light in his £60,000 Chevrolet sportscar. The 29-year-old Brazilian striker was recorded by a camera mounted on the A41 in Hendon, north London, driving his Chevrolet Corvette Stingray through traffic signals 1.5 seconds after they had turned red at 6.45pm on 15 April. At a hearing conducted behind closed doors at Barkingside Magistrates’ Court last week, the Premier League footballer was convicted of failing to comply with a red light signal. He was given a £200 fine, three penalty points on his licence, and ordered to pay £120 in prosecution costs alongside an £80 victim surcharge. Court papers reveal the Metropolitan Police gave the player options to avoid criminal prosecution for the traffic offence on the A41. A police worker told the court that Richarlison confirmed in writing that he was driving the car when it was filmed running the red light. The Met stated that Richarlison was offered the chance to take a driver retraining course, which he did not accept. He was then permitted to settle the matter by paying a fine; however, while he transferred the money, he failed to submit a copy of his driving licence. Richarlison has been frozen out by Robert De Zerbi (Getty) Consequently, Richarlison was prosecuted using the Single Justice Procedure, entering a written guilty plea without providing any mitigation for the offence. Richarlison was a key figure in Tottenham’s successful bid for Premier League survival last season. However, the striker has been frozen out under Roberto De Zerbi this term, following a proposed move back to former club Everton that fell through at the 11th hour. He has not featured for Tottenham since starting their 3-0 loss to Brentford on the opening day of the season. Richarlison has spent the last four years at Spurs since joining from Everton back in 2022. He also has 54 caps for Brazil, and has scored 20 goals for his country. However, he has not played for Brazil since October 2025 after falling out of favour with manager Carlo Ancelotti ahead of the World Cup earlier this year.

item.title: Brewers Join 2019 Nationals As Only Teams In History To Do This
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Sal Frelick The Milwaukee Brewers are 2-0 in the World Series against the Tampa Bay Rays. Both teams are trying to win their first World Series, but for the Brewers, they are in the World Series for the first time since 1982. Their franchise has been long deprived of even the experience of the World Series, and they are making the most of it. The Brewers surprised every baseball fan by sweeping the Los Angeles Dodgers and are now going to Tampa Bay with a chance to win the World Series. They are on a seven-game winning streak going back to Game 4 of the National League Division Series, which is longer than any of their regular-season win streaks. The last six wins are of some note, though. According to Just Baseball , this year's Brewers are the second team in MLB history to sweep the Championship Series and then win the first two games of the World Series. The only other team to do so was the 2019 Nationals, who went on to win the World Series in seven games. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! The Nationals lost Games 3, 4 and 5 of the 2019 World Series before winning the final two games on the road against the Houston Astros. The Brewers have not lost a home game since Sept. 13 and have three road wins this postseason. They will hope to avoid having to come back to Milwaukee to win it all. History seems to be on their side, and they are red hot this month. It feels like no lead is safe against them, and their pitching has been phenomenal, especially the bullpen. Payton Pritchard has established himself as one of the Boston Celtics ’ most reliable offensive weapons, but receiving praise from an NBA legend like Allen Iverson is a different kind of recognition. According to ESPN’s Hallie Grossman, Iverson approached Pritchard during the 2026 playoffs and delivered a memorable compliment to the Celtics guard: “You’re the coldest white boy I’ve ever seen.” Pritchard recalled the encounter after spotting Iverson, who stood out in an all-black outfit accented by a flashy Roman numeral III necklace. He has also become a trusted option in high-pressure situations, showing that he can deliver when Boston needs a timely basket. Praise from opposing players and other NBA figures can offer a glimpse into how a player’s skills are viewed around the league. Iverson’s comment is especially notable because his own game was defined by the same type of creativity and individual shot-making that Pritchard brings to the court. Pritchard has earned his reputation through his performances, but receiving that kind of endorsement from Iverson is a moment worth remembering. After signing a two-year extension with Boston , the guard won’t be going anywhere any time soon. item.title: WS Game 3 Preview
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - OCTOBER 19: A general view of Tropicana Field during Game Six of the American League Championship Series between the Cleveland Guardians and the Tampa Bay Rays on Monday, October 19, 2026 in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images This series has been amazing for casual baseball fans and those supporting the Milwaukee Brewers but it’s been infuriatingly brutal for those behind the Tampa Bay Rays. The first two games have been filled with costly mistakes and nearly almosts and the end result is the Rays being down two games to none against the team with the best record in baseball. Milwaukee has nearly been unbeatable this postseason with their only loss thus far coming against the San Diego Padres in game three of the NLDS. For the Rays to have any chance of getting back into the series, they’ll have to have a masterful performance from the ALCS MVP, Freddy Peralta. Peralta, 30, has been among the best pitchers in baseball over the past two months and found a new gear on his fastball since the playoffs began. Earlier this season, Peralta was averaging 94 mph on his fastball but that is up to 96.9 during his four playoff outings thus far. This was Peralta’s 9th season in the big leagues and over that time, he has only thrown 10 pitches at or above 99mph, 5 of them have been this postseason with the highest of his career (99.4) coming during his last time out in the 5th inning against Cleveland in game six. Perhaps facing his old team will allow him to find one more gear and reach triple digits. The Rays and Peralta will have to battle Robert Gasser, a southpaw drafted by the San Diego Padres as the 71st overall selection of the 2021 draft. Gasser was acquired by the Brewers in the lamented trade that sent Josh Hader to San Diego in 2022; now those with bad opinions on that deal may revise their judgement as Gasser could help to clinch the Brewers’ first World Series title in history. The 2026 season was Gasser’s longest time spent in the big leagues as he had short stints in 2024 and 2025. The 27-year was up and down this season until being brought up for good after the All-Star break. Over 21 games — 20 starts — this season, Gasser has a 3.87 ERA | 4.23 FIP with a 22.2 K% & 7.6 BB% over 109.1 IP. Thus far in the postseason, Gasser has pitched in 2 games, and has been incredible allowing just 1 run over nine innings of work. An observation from the previous games is that the Brewers hittes are tenacious with two strikes in the count. During the two World Series games thus far, the Brewers are hitting .182/.308/.333 with two strikes and have a 16.4 whiff%. Compare that to the regular season, the Brewers whiff rate was at 23.5% while the Rays led the MLB with a 21.0 two strike whiff%; that has jumped to 27.1% this postseason. item.description: Sal Frelick celebrates after hitting the game-tying home run in the sixth inning of Game 2 of the World Series, on the ninth pitch of the at-bat. (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) Getty Images Jake Bauers made a name for himself in the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers with his epic at-bats. First there was the 12-pitch walk against Yoshinobu Yamamoto in the third inning of Game 2. And then there was the 11-pitch battle against Blake Snell in the seventh inning of Game 3 that ended with the ball in the right field bleachers. But it would be short-sighted to think that Bauers is alone in his “ grind ‘em out ” approach to the Brewers’ at-bats. Each time they step into the batter’s box, they are trying to win a war of attrition. And they have kept that going in the first two games of the World Series. One exception to their rule may be left fielder Jackson Chourio, who loves to ambush the first pitch . He did it again on the first one Milwaukee saw in the Fall Classic, smashing a single to right. But then Bauers did what he does best, fighting a seven-pitch battle before flying out. Christian Yelich followed with a five-pitch at-bat of his own, which culminated with a run-scoring triple. In the seventh inning, with Steven Matz of the Tampa Rays out for his second frame, Cooper Pratt worked an eight-pitch lead-off walk. The rest of the hitters that inning were pretty typical, but the lead-off walk came around to score the third and eventual winning run. In Game 2, Milwaukee found themselves down 4-0 before they even put on their batting helmets. But they battled in the bottom of the first, sending seven men to the plate, scoring two runs to cut the lead in half, and forcing Rays’ ace Drew Rasmussen to throw 29 pitches. The Brewers went 1-2-3 in the second, but Jackson Chourio saw eleven two-out pitches before grounding out, causing Rasmussen to throw another 19, moving him to 48 to record just six outs. In the third, Bauers and Yelich both struck out, but saw 13 pitches in the process. By the time the Rays walked off the field, their starter had thrown 66 pitches. Pratt worked a seven-pitch walk with one out in the fourth. And after Bauers got a six-pitch walk with two outs, Rasmussen was done, having thrown 89 pitches over just 3-2/3 innings. In the sixth, trailing 4-3, Sal Frelick led-off, fouled off four of five pitches, and then hit the ninth offering to dead center field for a game-tying, roof-rattling home run. item.title: How Jalen Williams’ gruesome leg injury could alter Thunder’s title hopes
item.description: It became clear it was so bad – even in the first seconds after it happened – that a trainer rushed over to throw a towel over the ankle, hiding it from view. Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams, a 2024-25 All-Star and one of the bright young players in the NBA, suffered a seemingly devastating lower leg injury Sunday, Oct. 26. And though the Thunder haven’t issued a formal diagnosis, the way Williams’ left ankle dangled sideways off his foot strongly suggests that Williams’ season is over just three games after it started. So now the Thunder, who entered the season as favorites to win NBA Finals, must regroup, because this injury – assuming it’s as bad as it looked – changes the pathway for Oklahoma City moving forward. Because the overwhelming notion for this Thunder team was that it was a strong favorite because Williams was finally healthy. Williams, the team’s second best player, missed significant chunks last season as he recovered from offseason wrist surgery. Then, late in the year and into the playoffs, it was multiple soft-tissue hamstring injuries . So now, two-time reigning Most Valuable Player Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , once again, will have bear more of a burden. Williams can handle the ball and initiate offense. He can slash to the basket and has a dependable perimeter jumper. He’s a plus defender and is often the anchor through which the Thunder run their offense when Gilgeous-Alexander is catching a breath on the bench. When available, he is a staple, having started 238 of his 251 career regular season games. The loss is massive. "These are tough, man," Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said after the game. "We’re not doing great. That’s tough on the guys. Everyone empathizes, I think both teams, in those situations. We’re not doing great." Yet, if there is any team in the NBA built to weather the loss of a player like Williams, it’s the Thunder. No team has been better at identifying and developing young players through the draft, and Oklahoma City is the deepest team in the entire association. They have options. Thunder's depth provides options after Jalen Williams injury In fact, the Thunder are so deep that they can alter whom they start at small forward in place of Williams, depending on the matchup. The first indication of how the Thunder plan to make up for the loss of Williams comes fewer than 24 hours after he suffered the injury; Oklahoma City hosts the Phoenix Suns Monday, Oct. 26 on the second leg of their back-to-back. The cleanest move is for Daigneault to replace Williams in the starting lineup with Alex Caruso , a veteran guard who specializes on defense. Caruso is nowhere near as talented as Williams on offense, though his perimeter shot has been a spark off the bench; Caruso is shooting a blistering 45.5% from 3-point range this season. item.description: Michael Carrick has finally arrived at Carrington as Man United chiefs close to a decision on his future Manchester United are on the verge of another potential managerial sacking if all the latest reports are to be believed. Results under Michael Carrick this season have been abysmal, with the Red Devils winning only two games out of 12 in all competitions. The team have hardly displayed any real grit or determination on the pitch, regularly being outrun and outfought by the opposition, while the head coach’s tactics have been questionable to say the least. The former United midfielder is not the only one at fault here, with INEOS’ poor summer recruitment also to blame. Carrick arrives at Carrington However, Sir Jim Ratcliffe seems to trust director of football Jason Wilcox despite his horrendous track record. The former Manchester City academy chief reportedly wants Carrick out, with Eddie Howe his preferred candidate . As already relayed by The Peoples Person , Wilcox and club CEO Omar Berrada are at Carrington as crisis talks deepen. Now, The Manchester Evening News has reported that Carrick is also at United’s training ground. Crisis talks deepen The club have claimed that the head coach is there to watch the club’s Under-21s in action in a behind-closed-doors friendly, but that is unlikely to be the only reason for his arrival. “Michael Carrick has arrived at Carrington to watch Manchester United’s Under-21s in action as club chiefs continue to hold talks over his future. “United’s Under-21s are playing a behind-closed-doors friendly against Hull City on Monday afternoon and Carrick is set to attend. He arrived at the training ground at approximately 1.50pm. “Carrick will watch the U21s play in a friendly while Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox weigh up his future. Both Berrada and Wilcox are at Carrington, having reported to the training ground for crisis talks this morning.” Replacement options identified Among United’s other managerial targets is Antonio Conte, but the Italian wants full control over the club’s recruitment plans. That might put INEOS off. Howe remains eager to take over, while recruitment chief Christopher Vivell wants Julian Nagelsmann. It will be interesting to see when the final decision is revealed.

item.title: Mark McMorris And Red Gerard: From Podium Battles To X Games Teammates
item.description: Bronze medalist Red Gerard of the United States and gold medalist Mark McMorris of Canada celebrate after competing in the Men’s Snowboard Slopestyle on day three of the X Games Aspen 2026 at Buttermilk Ski Resort on January 25, 2026 in Aspen, Colorado. Getty Images There’s no question two of slopestyle snowboarding’s defining riders are Canada’s Mark McMorris and the United States’ Red Gerard. item.title: Cameron Young was closer to joining LIV Golf than anyone knew
item.description: In 2022, Cameron Young acknowledged he had seriously considered leaving the PGA Tour for LIV Golf . What he didn’t reveal was just how close he came. New bankruptcy records filed by LIV Golf show Young had signed an offer of intent with the breakaway league before ultimately deciding to remain with the PGA Tour. Young’s near-departure is one of several revelations contained in the financial records, which offer a deeper look at the money LIV spent on players and executives before filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection Sept. 8. "Obviously it's the elephant in the room for everyone. Frankly, throughout the whole process with (LIV Golf), I was very interested. I think they have a bunch of good ideas and are doing some cool stuff," Young said in August 2022. "With some of the changes coming (to the PGA Tour), that's kind of what really helped me decide to kind of stay and pursue those goals that I have for myself like making a Presidents Cup team and a Ryder Cup team and winning a major, when all of that is just uncertain if you go. That's a tough place for me because, you know, I'm very young and there are a lot of factors." Ultimately, Young stayed with the PGA Tour and has since won three times, including the 2026 Players Championship. He stands second on the 2026 PGA Tour money list with more than $15 million in earnings . The records also revealed that Greg Norman, LIV Golf’s former commissioner and CEO, received more than $9.4 million when he left the league in September 2025, including a settlement of about $5.8 million and a $3.6 million bonus. His successor, Scott O’Neil, received a $6.375 million retention bonus on June 24, less than three months before LIV filed for bankruptcy. That followed another bonus of approximately $2.7 million on Feb. 13. From Sept. 12, 2025, through Aug. 28, O’Neil received more than $13.6 million in payroll, bonuses, benefits, retention payments and expense reimbursements, according to the court records. All told, LIV paid approximately $15.6 million in retention payments to top executives. Chief financial officer David Phillips received more than $3.3 million, while chief legal officer John Ruzich received about $2.6 million. Those figures have surfaced as LIV tries to determine whether it has a future at all. LIV Golf and its related entities voluntarily filed for Chapter 11 protection Sept. 8, listing between $100 million and $500 million in assets and $500 million to $1 billion in liabilities. The league has since been laying the groundwork for LIV 2.0, a reworked version of the circuit that could be backed by London-based private-equity firm BC Partners. U.S. Bankruptcy Court Judge Michael B. Kaplan permitted LIV to enter into a restructuring plan with BC Partners that could provide as much as $300 million in financing, including an initial $4 million loan to help keep the league operating during the Chapter 11 process. item.description: ORLANDO, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 24: Bear Bachmeier #47 of the BYU Cougars scores a touchdown in the first half of the game between the UCF Knights and BYU Cougars at Acrisure Bounce House on October 24, 2026 in Orlando, Florida. (Photo by Dustin Markland/Getty Images) | Getty Images Week 8 of the college football season picked up right where Week 7 left it. Four of the top 11 teams in the AP Top 25 lost on Saturday, throwing another layer of chaos into the playoff picture. This season is starting to have a 2007-like feel to it, where no team is immune to an upset. My playoff picture after Week 8 is as follows: P4 Champions: Miami, Georgia, Ohio State, Utah G6 Leader: Boise State At-Larges: Indiana, Notre Dame, UCLA, BYU, Kentucky, Alabama, Texas Outside Looking In: Ole Miss, Texas Tech, Wake Forest, LSU, Tennessee Some notes from Week 8: James Madison has almost completely eliminated itself from the G6 race with a loss to Appalachian State. Boise State is clearly in the driver’s seat as the only G6 team in the AP poll. New Mexico received 41 votes, so do not count out the Lobos. But Boise State controls its fate for the G6 berth. Kentucky may be the biggest beneficiary of the Week 8 chaos, as the Wildcats jumped three spots after defeating Vanderbilt. Road games against Tennessee and Missouri, as well as a home game against Florida, remain on the team’s SEC schedule, but Kentucky has two weeks to get ready for it with a Halloween bye week. The Big Ten is a complete mess. The two remaining teams without a loss in conference play are UCLA and Ohio State, and both of them are on their backup quarterbacks. Indiana has offensive concerns and a banged up Josh Hoover, but the remaining schedule is very favorable. BYU lost a lot of breathing room with its 39-31 road loss to UCF, but that win over Notre Dame is still in their back pocket. The Cougars face Arizona State on Saturday, but the Holy War feels more like a must-win game for BYU than it did a week ago. Do not count out Wake Forest, who is quietly 6-1 with its only loss coming to Miami. The Demon Deacons have Virginia and Merrimack at home the next two weeks, but a key road game against SMU looms on November 14. There is a non-zero possibility we are talking about Wake Forest as an at-large team at Thanksgiving. The highest-ranked team with two losses that is not from the SEC is Houston (No. 18). Six of the seven two-loss SEC teams are higher than No. 18. The bias toward the conference is as large as ever. If you are Texas Tech, Wake Forest, SMU, Northwestern, BYU, or even unbeaten Utah and UCLA, you want to see those two-loss teams become three-loss teams as soon as possible. You need to keep winning, but it is clear that just having fewer losses than this logjam of SEC teams will not be sufficient.

item.title: Former Barcelona star praises Mourinho’s tactical masterclass in El Clasico win
item.description: Former Barcelona star praises Mourinho’s tactical masterclass in El Clasico win Real Madrid’s victory over Barcelona on Sunday was more than just three points in the La Liga title race. It was an important statement from Jose Mourinho, who outcoached Hansi Flick and made tactical decisions that helped his side overcome the Catalan giants. Barça came into this fixture looking unstoppable in the league, but Madrid’s 2-1 victory at Camp Nou has earned Jose considerable praise. Abelardo praises Mourinho’s midfield set-up As quoted by Defensa Central , former Barcelona player Abelardo Fernandez was particularly impressed by Madrid’s organisation. “Mourinho’s tactical approach in Barcelona was very good, with that 4-5-1 or 4-1-4-1,” Abelardo said. The 56-year-old highlighted the decision to position Aurelien Tchouameni behind Jude Bellingham and Bernardo Silva, giving Madrid greater balance through the middle. Jude Bellingham had an outrageous game against Barcelona’s midfield. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) With Tchouameni providing defensive protection, his teammates had more freedom to support attacks without leaving the back line completely exposed. Abelardo was especially impressed by Bellingham, whose contribution went beyond his attacking responsibilities. “We talk about many Madrid players, but Bellingham’s performance was spectacular,” he explained. The Englishman won 13 duels during the encounter , more than Barcelona’s entire midfield combined. Such numbers underline how good he was on the night. Jose Mourinho exploited Barcelona’s weakness Abelardo also explained how Barcelona’s defensive problems contributed to Madrid’s success on the night. “I think Barcelona also lost because, defensively, they are a very vulnerable team,” he explained. This, in principle, was one of the main foundations of Mourinho’s tactical set-up last night. Los Blancos did not need to dominate possession to outplay their opponents. Tchouameni’s positioning, along with the intelligence and energy of Bellingham and Bernardo, helped Real Madrid outplay Barça in midfield. Aurelien Tchouameni was excellent in the middle of the park for Madrid. (Photo by Tullio M. Puglia/Getty Images) It is a particularly encouraging result for Los Blancos because of how much they had struggled against Barcelona in recent meetings. Mourinho’s team showed last night that they could adapt to Flick’s aggressive style rather than simply attempting to match it. The victory has now reduced Madrid’s gap to their arch-rivals to just three points, throwing the title race wide open. Mourinho’s Real Madrid will now strive for consistency and hope to perform at a similar level in the coming weeks to keep the pressure on Barcelona in La Liga.

But on October 26, Lindor received an honor that has little to do with his numbers at the plate or his performance on the field. The New York Mets star was named the 2026 recipient of the Roberto Clemente Award, Major League Baseball’s highest individual honor for a player’s character, philanthropy and community impact. Growing up in Puerto Rico, he learned about Clemente’s career and humanitarian efforts in school. Lindor has spoken about how Clemente inspired him to use his own platform to help others. Lindor is the fifth Puerto Rican-born player to win the award, joining Edgar Martínez, Carlos Delgado, Carlos Beltrán and Yadier Molina. That connection makes this recognition particularly significant. Puerto Rico has a rich baseball tradition, and Clemente remains one of its most influential figures. (Photo by Todd Olszewski/Getty Images) | Getty Images Offense QB: Tyler Huntley 67 RB: Derrick Henry 34, Justice Hill 31, Rasheen Ali 4 WR: Zay Flowers 57, Rashod Bateman 49, Ja’Kobi Lane 46, Devontez Walker 20, LaJohntay Wester 1 TE: Mark Andrews 38, Matthew Hibner 26, Josh Cuevas 15, Nick Vannett 14 OL: Ronnie Stanley 67, John Simpson 67, Cam Jurgens 67, Vega Ioane 16, Emery Jones Jr. 51 The Ravens played 67 offensive snaps and again did not receive a full showing from their starting offensive line because of injuries. Vega Ioane was replaced by Emery Jones Jr. after he suffered a knee injury and did not return to the game. Jones played the final 51 snaps at right guard next to Cam Jurgens, who started at center for the first time since being traded to the Ravens. Jurgens played the entire game. In the backfield, it was a near-evens split between Derrick Henry and Justice Hill. Unfortunately, the Ravens were ineffective running the ball again. Henry averaged less than 3.0 yards per carry on 17 attempts and with the team trailing big late in the game, Rasheen Ali played four snaps and had four carries. Matthew Hibner returned from injury at tight end and reassumed his No. 2 role in the pecking order. He was not targeted in the passing game, however. Josh Cuevas had 35 receiving yards on two catches in 15 snaps, while fourth-stringer Nick Vannett played 14 snaps as a blocker. Mark Andrews was quiet with only three receptions for minimal yardage in 38 snaps. The only offensive bright spot was, once again, Zay Flowers. In 57 snaps, Flowers had eight catches for 137 yards with a long touchdown. This was the first game in which Flowers, Rashod Bateman and Ja’Kobi Lane all played together for four quarters. Bateman slightly out-snapped Lane (49 to 46), with Devontez Walker sliding down into a clear No. 4 role with 20 snaps. item.title: Ben Stiller agrees with New York Knicks fan opinion on key problem facing NBA champions right now
item.description: Photo by Emilee Chinn/Getty Images Actor Ben Stiller seems to agree with a New York Knicks fan after the team’s third straight loss of the season. The defending champions fell to a 0-3 start after another poor performance, this time against the Orlando Magic. Going into the final 12 minutes, the Knicks had a four-point lead, but they ended up conceding 40 points in the fourth quarter, which led to a 111-102 loss. Knicks Fan TV’s CP “The Franchise” shared his analysis of the game on X, where he said: “The Knicks were stumbling and bumbling, too many turnovers again, seven turnovers in the fourth quarter alone. They’ve given up 23 points off turnovers tonight, 22 points off turnovers in game one against Philly and 19 points off of turnovers against the Celtics.” He then went on to add that the turnover problem has compounded the transition defence being an issue for the Knicks. Ben Stiller also thinks the Knicks are struggling with turnovers Stiller, who is one of the most famous Knicks fans, shared the clip on his X account and simply said: “Yes.” That was enough to summarise the turnover struggles the team has faced this season. In the game against the Magic, they gave away 8 turnovers in the fourth quarter alone. They had a 10-point lead at one stage during the fourth quarter, but the constant turnovers took the game away from them. Brunson has given up 2.7 turnovers per game, while Karl-Anthony Towns has 4 per game to his name. These are two of the highest scorers on the team, which is why it is essential that they take care of the ball better. “It’s the focus on the details,” head coach Mike Brown said. “We throw the ball down here, it goes through our hands, and we jump in there and throw, you know, and those turnovers, they convert the other way.” The Knicks next play the Detroit Pistons on Tuesday. With Ausar Thompson as a defender, the Knicks cannot afford to do anything silly with the ball. If they are able to contain their turnover problem and their stars put in a big performance, the defending champions could get their first win of the season. item.title: How Shane Lowry’s short game advice could take amateur golfers’ chipping to another level
item.description: Photo by Warren Little/Getty Images Shane Lowry undoubtedly possesses one of the best short games in the world. Sure, Lowry’s technique is more natural than most, and his hands and wrists are far more active when he’s chipping than most players at the highest level of the game. However, there aren’t many better players at getting the ball up and down around the greens than the Irishman. What makes Shane Lowry so good is the simplicity with which he chips and pitches the ball. Amateur golfers could learn so much from the way the 2019 Open champion goes about things around the greens. Shane Lowry’s short game advice could take your chipping to another level Lowry took part in a short game instructional video for Golf Digest and revealed how he wants to limit his options around the greens as much as possible. “ I only chip with two clubs really. I use my lob wedge the majority of the time, and then the odd time, I’ll chip and run, but only with a pitching wedge, “ the Irishman said. “ I don’t want to do anything else. I find the big thing for me is, when I’m chipping, I find that if I have too many options, I get, like, in between shots. Like, I used to carry four wedges. So, I’d have a 52, 56 and a 60 and a wedge. “ Then, on the odd time, I’d chip with my 56, but then I’d have too many options, and I get, like, in between shots. “ Then I wouldn’t hit any of them how I wanted to, so I’d end up being a bit sloppy. Whereas now, like, I practice with my pitching wedge, and I practice with my lob wedge. “ I don’t use anything else. I just find that gives me more clarity of what I want to do in my head. “ Amateur golfers really should take a leaf out of Shane Lowry’s book. Any amateur looking to improve their short game should focus on mastering one specific chip shot around the greens. Obviously there will be times when the shot you face requires a completely different approach. For example, if there is a bunker between your ball and the hole, you will obviously need to keep the ball up in the air for the majority of its journey. However, you should only require one club to chip and pitch the ball with for the vast majority of the time. This takes away any kind of indecision and if you focus your practice solely on chipping with one specific club, you should naturally improve as a chipper anyway. If that method is good enough for Shane Lowry, it really should be good enough for us.
